method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: Both sheets letter the corridor in the roadway: sheet 49 view 1 and view 2 print 'AVE. G OR WINNIE' vertically in it, and sheet 55 view 1 and view 2 print the identical 'AVE. G OR WINNIE'. The hundred-block runs on the cross streets confirm it on each sheet independently. Sheet 49: the block west of the corridor carries 601-623 odd / 602-624 even along 26th and 27th Sts (600 block), the block east of it carries 701-723 / 702-724 (700 block), and the next corridor east (lettered 'AVE. H OR BALL') starts the 800 block (801-823 / 802-824, seen in view 3). Sheet 55: identical structure - 619-623 / 620-624 west of the corridor, 701-723 / 702-724 east of it, and 801-823 / 802-824 east of the next corridor, which is again lettered 'AVE. H OR BALL' (view 3), with 'AVE. I OR SEALY' beyond that. So on both sheets the hundred-block series starts anew at each lettered avenue (F=600, G=700, H=800, I=900) and the chosen line is the one that breaks 600 from 700 on both. One block west is Ave F (Church) - excluded because it is lettered 'AVE. F OR CHURCH' on both sheets (sheet 49 view 1 at native ~148, sheet 55 view 1 at native ~144) and it breaks 500 from 600, not 600 from 700. One block east is Ave H (Ball) - excluded because it is lettered 'AVE. H OR BALL' on both sheets (sheet 49 ~2155.5, sheet 55 ~2151.2) and it breaks 700 from 800. The line the red marker fell on is not an avenue at all: it is the 20 ft mid-block alley carrying the dashed 6" W. PIPE (measured 60 native px = 19.8 ft, versus 212 native px = 70 ft for the avenue roadway), and the addresses do not change hundreds across it (701-711 continue 713-723). Cross-check on the identification: the sheet-49-minus-sheet-55 offset measured independently on Ave G is +3.8 px and on Ave H is +4.3 px, agreeing to under half a pixel; a one-avenue misidentification would have produced a ~1004 px discrepancy between the two. MEASUREMENT: Native x is the roadway CENTRELINE, the midpoint of the two block street-casing lines, located to sub-pixel precision by an intensity-weighted centroid with a per-row adaptive ink threshold, read against the green native-pixel ruler (calibration verified on every crop: the labelled long ticks land within 1 px of exact multiples of 500). Sheet 49 Ave G casings: west 1048.5 (view 1) / 1048.0 (view 2), east 1256.7 / 1256.0 -> centre 1152.3, roadway width 208.1 native px = 68.7 ft at the sheet scale of 3.03 px/ft, matching the printed 70' label in the corridor. Sheet 55 Ave G casings: west 1041.8 / 1041.3, east 1253.1 / 1251.4 -> centre 1146.9, width 210.7 native px = 69.6 ft. Every casing was read on two independent views and agreed to about 1 px. Consistency check on the identification: the sheet-49-minus-sheet-55 offset is +5.4 px on Ave G and +4.3 px on Ave H (sheet 49 ~2155, sheet 55 ~2151); a one-avenue misidentification would have produced a ~1004 px discrepancy between the two.
